purpose: Clarify what the existing Windows-shaped RAW10 converter's 0/90-degree modes actually test.

operations: Unpack MIPI RAW10 and retain the high eight bits.
Generate split geometry for engine orientation inputs 0 and 90 degrees.

results.visualInspection: Contrast stretching shows a broad horizontal boundary and mostly fine grain, with no identifiable eye detail.

interpretation: The --rotation option name was misleading: the converter models the Windows engine's orientation-dependent split axis/order, not physical rotation of the pixel matrix. The two full-frame outputs being byte-identical confirms this. The earlier wording that candidate rotations 0 and 90 were decoded did not establish or test native Cityman sensor orientation. The orientation mapping and Windows tone normalization remain unresolved.
privacy: Raw and rendered pixels remain in /private/tmp outside the repository. No image pixels are included in this record.
publication: local only; no commit, push, or PR
